title: The 10 Largest Bankruptcies Of All Time
主要内容: MF Global Holdings Ltd (OTC: MFGLQ) collapsed in 2009 after the brokerage made a $6.3 billion bet on European sovereign debt. Energy Future Holdings Corp filed for bankruptcy in 2014 after the company's big bets on natural gas failed to pay off. Conseco's problems stemmed from an ill-advised purchase of mobile homes financier Green Tea Financial in 1998. Rampant fraud within the energy-trading company led to Enron's infamous stock slide and subsequent bankruptcy. CIT Group (2009) filed for bankruptcy during the credit crunch in 2009 due to inability to find funding. The commercial lender had $80.4 billion in assets. General Motors (2009) agreed to bankruptcy as part of its government bailout due to debt and unfavorable union deals. GM had $91.0 billion in assets. WorldCom (2002) filed for bankruptcy after a $4 billion accounting scandal, with $103.9 billion in assets. Washington Mutual (2008) collapsed due to a $16.7 billion nine-day withdrawal run, leaving the bank crippled. The company had $327.9 billion in assets. Lehman Brothers Holdings (2008) is the largest bankruptcy of all time with $691.1 billion in assets, serving as the poster child for the financial crisis.
